recommendation: Keep the source cleanup. If the project wants recurrence prevention, consider a separate human-approved publisher/style check that excludes imported external standards and non-built working notes.
issue_request: FHIR-13564 was Published/Persuasive for STU3 and requested that all uses of 'may not' be reviewed and changed to 'might not' for possibility or 'shall not' for prohibition because 'may not' can be misread as a conformance prohibition.
initial_application: The issue was applied in svn revision 12802, represented by git commit d33191d634a51afc60193ac498c314a9fd2a6c7f, titled '#13564 - hunt and destroy all uses of may not'. That commit changed 170 source files and updated the ValueSet wording called out in the Jira to 'might not'.
additional_context: Later R5/R6 edits reintroduced 'may not', 'MAY not', and 'MAY or MAY NOT' in active core source including resource StructureDefinition XML, resource narrative snippets, search/subscription narrative pages, examples, terminology source, and fhir.ini migration text. Remaining post-fix matches are imported DICOM text and an unreferenced StructureMap working note, which were left unchanged. FHIR-48870 introduced one later RelatedPerson occurrence and was treated as background only.
reconciliation: Changed non-prohibitive current FHIR-authored occurrences to 'might not' or 'might or might not' and changed the single apparent prohibitive 'may NOT' occurrence to 'SHALL NOT'. No conformance expectation was intentionally changed; the edits clarify wording consistent with FHIR-13564.
source_changes: source/subscriptions.html: Rephrased two out-of-band subscription statements from 'MAY or MAY NOT' to 'might or might not'.
source/subscription/subscription-notes.xml: Rephrased notification security wording to 'might or might not'.
source/subscriptionstatus/subscriptionstatus-notes.xml: Rephrased four additionalContext existence statements to 'might or might not'.
source/search.html: Rephrased self-link resolvability, resolved content type, and text sort support wording to avoid 'MAY or MAY NOT'/'may not'.

source/consent/structuredefinition-Consent.xml, source/encounter/structuredefinition-Encounter.xml, source/imagingselection/structuredefinition-ImagingSelection.xml, source/imagingstudy/structuredefinition-ImagingStudy.xml: Rephrased active resource definitions/comments to use 'might not' or 'might or might not'.
source/encounter/encounter-event-mapping-exceptions.xml: Kept the Encounter mapping exception text aligned with the Encounter.subject definition change.
source/patient/operation-Patient-merge-notes.xml and source/diagnosticreport/diagnosticreport-examples-lab-text.xml: Rephrased user-facing operation/example text to 'might not'.
source/relatedperson/relatedperson-introduction.xml: Rephrased the apparent prohibition from 'may NOT' to 'SHALL NOT'.
source/terminologies/codesystem-template-lifecycle.xml and source/fhir.ini: Rephrased terminology and migration note text to avoid 'may or may not'/'may not'.
